r0041: I.  ALLEGED VIOLATION OF ARTICLE 1 OF PROTOCOL No. 1
r0042: 23.  The applicant complained that his prolonged inability to recover possession of his apartment, owing to the failure to provide police assistance, had infringed his right to property as guaranteed by Article 1 of Protocol No. 1 to the Convention, which provides:
r0043: “Every natural or legal person is entitled to the peaceful enjoyment of his possessions. No one shall be deprived of his possessions except in the public interest and subject to the conditions provided for by law and by the general principles of international law.
r0044: The preceding provisions shall not, however, in any way impair the right of a State to enforce such laws as it deems necessary to control the use of property in accordance with the general interest or to secure the payment of taxes or other contributions or penalties.”
r0046: 24.  The Court, relying on its case-law, considers that the interference complained of by the applicant amounts to a control of the use of property within the meaning of Article 1 of Protocol No. 1 (see Immobiliare Saffi, cited above, § 46).
r0047: B.  Compliance with the conditions laid down in the second paragraph
r0049: 25.  The Court has already held that the legislation in issue pursued a legitimate aim in the general interest, as required by the second paragraph of Article 1 (see Immobiliare Saffi, cited above, § 48).
